note: Track P packages. Parity is a gate on every node: acceptance names (a) the metric improvement, (b) the parity artifact that proves nothing was degraded, (c) the states/viewports compared. Missing parity annuls a package regardless of numbers (owner amendment OI-2026-11-02-PERF-PARITY). Contract: docs/track-p-performance-parity.md.

slices.title: Baseline measurement + UX Surface Manifest + parity harness + detector calibration
slices.acceptance: (a) metric: baseline B (deployed SHA) cold/warm/desktop p50+p95 for time-to-useful-Status, interactive first screen, control response, long tasks, frame drops, request count, transfer bytes, 304 share, SQL count+EXPLAIN, JSON size, event-loop lag; (b) parity: UX Surface Manifest + parity matrix artifacts for B captured by the same runner that will capture C, and detector calibration on a throwaway copy (one effect disabled => manifest counters drop and metrics rise) proven; (c) states/viewports: 320x700, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800 + regression sweep from tools/ui_round1025_matrix.py VIEWPORTS; states cold first frame, Status useful screen, each tab, chat/scope switch, .more-sheet closed/open, fullscreen normal/fullscreen, glass tiers a/b/c/shell on the stand, reduced-motion.
slices.why_one_slice: One runner, one environment, one baseline: splitting it would produce traces that cannot be compared and would break the single-SHA contract.

slices.title: R1 — HTTP delivery, cache policy, ETag/304, compression, CSP
slices.acceptance: (a) metric: 304 share on warm entry up, transfer bytes down, time-to-useful-Status down, post-release load without forced cache clear; (b) parity: decompressed served JS/CSS/HTML bytes identical to baseline, 0-px geometry, control/DOM inventory, INV-GLASS/INV-POLY/INV-MOTION and INV-DATA artifacts equal, P-04 stale-mixed-asset run passing; (c) states/viewports: 320x700, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800 + sweep; second entry same release, new release after deploy, GET/HEAD/ETag/304 path. No parity artifact => package not acceptable.
slices.why_one_slice: A single delivery-policy surface (web/app.py) with one observable outcome (reuse without stale mix); it cannot be split by endpoint, but it must not absorb script-order or frontend work.

slices.title: R2 — request dedup/orchestration, bootstrap staging, stale-response guard, scoped memo
slices.acceptance: (a) metric: requests to useful screen, removed duplicate GETs, time-to-interactive, mutation count on retry (no duplicated writes); (b) parity: loading/error/empty/retry state inventory equal, INV-DATA/INV-DOM equal, P-06 no stale overwrite, P-13 conflict/revision with two admins, no secret/initData in browser storage; (c) states/viewports: 320x700, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800 + sweep; rapid chat switch, slow network, API failure, offline->online. No parity artifact => package not acceptable.
slices.why_one_slice: All request orchestration lives in one fetch/bootstrap layer; separate tickets would create two competing request paths and an untestable cache contract.

slices.title: R3 — script order/deferred loading, mount-on-demand, direct deep link, duplicate vendor removal
slices.acceptance: (a) metric: main-thread parse/compile/mount, long tasks, time to useful Status, deep-link load, no growth of listeners/timers/canvas/heap over repeated tab cycles; (b) parity: identical DOM after load on every tab and on deep links, no new interim placeholder where content previously appeared immediately, INV-DOM/INV-GLASS/INV-POLY/INV-MOTION/INV-ROUTE equal, keyboard/landscape/fullscreen/dropdown states intact, P-15 no CSP/auth/bridge/Chart/DOMPurify regression; (c) states/viewports: 320x700, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800 + sweep; each tab, deep link per tab, landscape 844x390, fullscreen, reduced-motion. No parity artifact => package not acceptable.
slices.why_one_slice: Script order and mount-on-demand are one coupled mechanism on one file pair: deferred loading without mount boundaries gives no win, and mount boundaries without load ordering reintroduce blocking parse.

slices.title: R6 — background/glass engines: batched reads/writes, idle when hidden, no double engines
slices.acceptance: (a) metric: frame drops, long tasks, idle CPU/GPU while document.hidden, per-frame layout count, no growth across tab cycles; (b) parity: all 11 getDiagnostics fields equal at fixed ?bgseed=, nodeCount inside 90-140 desktop / 45-75 mobile, bloom+motorphase present, INV-MOTION inventory and transform/opacity samples equal, INV-GLASS tiers/backdrop-filter/--glass-* tokens equal, 0-pixel diff for deterministic states, glass never disabled on any path; (c) states/viewports: 320x700, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800 + sweep; document.hidden round trip, closed modal, hidden overlay, fullscreen normal/fullscreen. No parity artifact => package not acceptable.
slices.why_one_slice: The five static engines share one rAF/ResizeObserver lifecycle and one visible picture; splitting them would allow one engine to keep rendering while another idles, which is exactly the wasted work this package removes.
slices.scope_extension_rule: If profiling proves the remaining waste is rAF/ResizeObserver code inside web/app.js, P4 returns a written scope-extension request to the orchestrator; it must NOT edit web/app.js while P3 owns it.

slices.title: R5 — /config split, proven N+1/EXPLAIN fixes, keyset pagination, event-loop relief
slices.acceptance: (a) metric: endpoint p50/p95, SQL statement count, EXPLAIN of the most expensive SELECT before/after, JSON payload bytes, event-loop lag; (b) parity: rendered row/field/value counts at a fixed dataset equal, same fields and reachability in the UI, param_catalog single source of truth, RBAC/effective values and write endpoints unchanged, no zero-substitution on timeout; (c) states/viewports: 320x700, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800 + sweep; tabs with many records, two-admin concurrent edit, pagination boundary pages. No parity artifact => package not acceptable.
slices.next_role: Builder, then Reviewer, then DevOps for indexes
slices.why_one_slice: One server-side measurement surface (endpoints+SQL) with one outcome (same data, less work); migrations are additive-only and belong to the same rollback story.
slices.scope_extension_rule: web/app.py endpoints are owned by P1-CACHE-DELIVERY; P5 must not edit web/app.py concurrently and instead files an explicit scope-extension request.

slices.title: Consolidated parity + attribution gate (release blocker) for the whole track
slices.acceptance: (a) metric: consolidated B->C delta table with one attributed internal cause per win (requests/304 share, bytes, SQL count, parse, duplicate GET, JSON size) and explicit HOLD when a win appears only where the UX Surface Manifest changed; (b) parity: consolidated parity pack (manifest diff shows no decrease, 0-px geometry, pixel diffs, functional runs, exclusion-list audit) for the same candidate SHA, plus proof that no lightweight mode/silent fallback/effect downgrade exists in the diff; (c) states/viewports: 320x700, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800 + sweep, all states listed for the packages. Any deviation annuls the release regardless of numbers.
slices.why_one_slice: One consolidated verdict over one candidate: parity is meaningless per-file, and this is the only place where the release blocker is declared.

slices.title: R4 — byte reduction (optional, deferred; needs build-step decision)
slices.acceptance: Deferred and NOT opened by default: only a zero-new-build byte reduction that keeps AST-identical behaviour and CSS token values may be proposed, with its own parity artifact at 320x700, 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x800; it can never substitute for a measured UI speed-up (DoD P).
slices.why_one_slice: Kept as an explicit, unopened lane so R4 is not silently forgotten and equally not smuggled in as a 'side effect' of R3.

slices.title: Track H — full Help rewrite (gate unchanged, NOT opened by track P)
slices.acceptance: H opens only when every earlier current_task item (including the whole E track and this P track) is implemented, Reviewer-passed, deployed and live-verified; the E-track nodes and any queue items added between must be appended to this graph as dependencies before H starts. Documentation is not edited before that gate.
slices.gate_note: Track H gating is unchanged by the parity amendment. This node exists so the H dependency is machine-visible; it is a placeholder for the H plan, not an authorisation to start.
slices.why_one_slice: H is a single editorial deliverable over two canon documents with one delivery path; its gate is the dependency, not internal slicing.
